newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo gold jewellery producer in export boost - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo gold jewellery producer in export boost - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest producer of gold jewellery Zlatara Majdanpek hopes to use reduced taxes and a barter deal with China to bring its exports to pre-1991 levels, Belgrade daily Politika said on Thursday.

"The government slashed excise duties from 50 to 15 percent and cut the sales tax from 24 to 20 percent, and that means a lot for our exports," the paper quoted general manager Filip Vukovic as saying.
This will make us more competitive both home and abroad, Vukovic added.
"Soon we aim to raise our monthly sales to 80 kilos of jewellery at home and 120 kilos abroad," Vukovic said.
Four years ago, Zlatara exported 1.5 tonnes of gold jewellery a year, earning around 15 million sterling. Then, total annual production stood at three tonnes, the paper said.
Increased exports of jewellery would mean lower sales of gold bullion from the Bor mining complex. Politika said sales of jewellery would bring earnings three times greater than bullion exports.
Zlatara said it was hopeful of participating in a barter deal with China, signed earlier this year. The deal involves exchanging Yugoslav products for about $1 billion in crude oil.
Zlatara expects to sell some 400 kgs of jewellery and 2,000 kgs of gold for plating to China, bringing the company around $10 million.

Estimated copper and gold reserves in the Bor-Majdanpek region stood at some 1,000 tonnes of gold and about 12 million tonnes of pure copper -- enough for another century of exploitation, Politika said.
